findings.description: CON-SUP-103 permits a task to start at the limit and defines a late start as later than the limit. Detecting a fault at expiry when the task has not started can also fault a start exactly at the limit.
findings.requested_change: Define detection and boundary handling so a start at the configured limit is accepted and a later start is detected, consistent with the specified measurement resolution.

findings.description: The trigger requires execution longer than the limit, but the response is required at the limit's expiry. The statement does not resolve whether completion exactly at the limit is accepted, as CON-SUP-103 requires.
findings.requested_change: Specify how the expiry detection distinguishes completion at the limit from execution beyond it, including the 100 µs measurement resolution.

findings.description: The trigger refers to an allowed range without identifying its contents or referencing CON-SUP-115, which identifies a limit longer than the task period, a zero period and an unknown task as configuration faults.
findings.requested_change: State or precisely reference the configuration conditions that trigger fault code 9.

findings.description: The unconditional refresh at the end of each cycle conflicts with SYS-SUP-013, which withholds every watchdog service action while a fault is detected. STK-SUP-005 permits servicing only while every supervised task is healthy.
findings.requested_change: Qualify the refresh obligation with the permitted health conditions and reconcile it with the fault reaction.

findings.description: The condition 'while a fault is detected' does not establish when withholding starts or ends, including whether it persists after detection until reset. STK-SUP-005 requires watchdogs to be serviced only while every supervised task is healthy.
findings.requested_change: Define the fault and health conditions that govern withholding and the event that ends it.

findings.description: The requirement detects a mismatch with a stored reference, but OP-SYS-004 leaves the reference and comparison method undefined. A verifier cannot determine which program changes must cause a mismatch or establish the expected result from the stated condition.

The unconditional instruction to drive status high when integrity checks pass can conflict with the safe-state latch in SYS-SUP-009 and SYS-SUP-028, which must remain in the safe state until power-on reset. CON-SUP-109 defines low as not operational.
findings.requested_change: Define the conditions for indicating operational status so that passing integrity checks cannot override a latched safe state.

findings.description: CON-SUP-110 requires transmission after entry into the safe state, whereas this requirement only sets a 10 ms deadline from detection and permits transmission before safe-state entry. SYS-SUP-022 allows up to 50 ms for entry.
findings.requested_change: Reconcile the required transmission order with both deadlines, recording a blocking decision if the input timing and ordering cannot be satisfied together.

findings.description: OP-SYS-006 leaves the origin and wrap behavior of 'ms since start' undecided. A verifier cannot determine the expected timestamp across resets or counter wrap.

The unconditional reset request after safe-state entry conflicts with SYS-SUP-009, which latches the safe state for an out-of-range configuration until power-on reset, and can conflict with SYS-SUP-028's repeated-fault latch.
findings.requested_change: Specify when the reset request is suppressed for a latched safe state, consistent with the product decisions.

findings.description: The required code 8 fault report has an entity field under SYS-SUP-024, but CON-SUP-112 does not define its value for a watchdog reset. OP-SYS-003 records the missing decision.
findings.requested_change: Define the report entity for fault code 8 after the product decision is made.

findings.description: OP-SYS-005 leaves the status state values and the meaning of fault count undefined. A verifier cannot determine the expected STS response for a given operating and reset history.
